inventor.match: Match each invention to its inventor.

rows.label: ibuprofen
rows.hook: is a common over-the-counter painkiller taken for headaches, fever and inflammation

rows.label: penicillin
rows.description: group of antibiotics derived from Penicillium fungi
rows.hook: was the first widely used antibiotic, discovered from a mould growing on a lab dish

rows.label: stainless steel
rows.description: chromium-containing steel alloy resistant to corrosion
rows.hook: is the rust-resistant alloy of iron and chromium used for cutlery and kitchen sinks

rows.label: nitroglycerin
rows.hook: is a highly unstable explosive oil that Alfred Nobel later tamed into dynamite

rows.label: aspartame
rows.hook: is a low-calorie artificial sweetener found in many diet sodas

rows.label: vaseline
rows.hook: is a brand of soft petroleum jelly used on dry skin and minor scrapes

rows.label: WD-40
rows.description: lubricating oil and water displacement spray
rows.hook: is a blue-and-yellow spray can used to loosen squeaky hinges and stuck bolts

rows.label: margarine
rows.description: semi-solid oily spread often used as a butter substitute
rows.hook: is a spread made from vegetable oils, created as a cheaper alternative to butter

rows.label: Bakelite
rows.hook: is regarded as the first fully synthetic plastic, used in old telephones and radios

rows.label: portland cement
rows.description: binder used as basic ingredient of concrete
rows.hook: is the fine grey powder mixed with sand and water to make most of the world's concrete

rows.label: nitrocellulose
rows.description: highly flammable compound formed by nitrating cellulose through exposure to nitric acid or to another nitrating agent
rows.hook: is the flammable material also called guncotton, used in early film and smokeless powder

rows.label: chlorofluorocarbon
rows.description: hydrocarbon derivative that contains only carbon, chlorine and fluorine
rows.hook: is the refrigerant and aerosol gas family blamed for damaging the ozone layer
